evidence.title: Claudette v0.29.0 README
evidence.locator: README.md Highlights, About, Command-line client, Remote access, Relationship to Anthropic
evidence.finding: The pinned README lists cross-platform desktop builds, parallel worktree sessions, a local IPC CLI, a separately installable user-hosted server, and a bundled Claude Code orchestration skill.

evidence.title: Claudette agent provider architecture
evidence.locator: Agent Providers lines 6–47 and provider setup/auth table
evidence.finding: Claude Code uses the official claude subprocess. Native Codex uses codex app-server over stdio; native Antigravity uses agy acp. OpenAI API and Ollama are model-provider routes through Claude-compatible/gateway paths, not additional coding harnesses.

evidence.title: Claudette authentication
evidence.locator: Authentication lines 6–54; Pro/Max plans and API keys
evidence.finding: Agent runs use the official Claude CLI credentials, including Pro/Max login or configured API keys. The Usage panel separately reads/refreshes OAuth credentials to query Anthropic usage; the no-token-reading statement is scoped to agent subprocess traffic, not every app feature.

evidence.title: Claudette native Codex login
evidence.finding: Codex uses the native app-server and codex login, with ChatGPT subscription access. The OpenAI API backend instead takes an API key and uses the local gateway.

evidence.title: Claudette product-owned scheduling
evidence.finding: Claudette owns persisted wakeups/cron routines and a GUI. It hides provider-native volatile scheduling tools when its own MCP bridge is attached. Missed tasks fire when the app restarts; background completion can re-invoke an agent.

evidence.title: Claudette diff interface
evidence.finding: The product documents real-time unified and side-by-side diffs, added/removed lines and layer-specific staged, unstaged, untracked and committed views.

evidence.title: Claudette displayed unified code diff
evidence.locator: Original image, center WorkspacePanelHeader.tsx diff under CHANGES
evidence.finding: The opened original displays added isMac and sidebarVisible source lines and a red/green replacement of the header div className. This is displayed code content rather than a changed-file count. The image shows PR 605 Ready to merge but does not itself prove merge authorization.

evidence.title: Claudette SCM provider workflow
evidence.finding: The SCM tab shows PR/CI state and Create PR/Merge PR actions through already-authenticated gh or glab. Optional CI failure handling can start a fresh agent session; permissions remain with the upstream CLI account.

evidence.title: Claudette privacy documentation
evidence.locator: Privacy, No Accounts; No Remote Servers; Network Activity
evidence.finding: The documentation states no app-vendor account and no vendor telemetry, analytics or crash reporting. This statement was read as documentation; this pass did not audit every analytics/crash dependency and does not publish a no-telemetry default or off-switch finding.

evidence.title: Claudette MIT license
evidence.finding: The main repository grants the client and included server code under MIT, free of charge. Third-party/provider components retain their own terms.

evidence.title: Inspected repository metadata
evidence.finding: Repository utensils/claudette has archived=false. This field alone does not establish an active product or service.

evidence.title: Default-branch commit snapshot
evidence.finding: Default-branch head 9e9f90611450471129b335652f2ae822a56348d8 has committer timestamp 2026-11-25T17:51:20Z. This is repository activity, not a service availability test.

evidence.locator: .claude/skills/claudette/SKILL.md quick start, Inspect and orchestrate chat sessions, and Fan out N workspaces
evidence.finding: The stable shipped skill grants the agent access to the product CLI and documents workspace creation, child-chat inspection, follow-up prompts, pending controls and batch fan-out. Its batch command processes workspaces sequentially; this does not establish parallel execution of that batch command.
